A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLoCE research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including content moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-erasure experiments, adversarial evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds SD v3, localized object-erasure, LEACE, additional attack, and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The low-rank projections, surrogate-centered gate, inference-only parameter estimation, and maximum-gate selection for multiple concepts remain unchanged. The SD v3 experiments do not introduce a documented new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds localized erasure of airplane and dog concepts from prompts containing target and remaining objects. This is a focused extension beyond the retained celebrity, artistic-style, explicit-content, character-preservation, and COCO coverage.

E2.justification: LEACE, previously discussed as theoretical groundwork, becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables D.4–D.6, including direct SD v1.4 celebrity comparisons. The original main-table comparator sets remain unchanged. Newly discussed CPE is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation settings with a DiT-based SD v3 backbone using 28 generation steps and additional PEZ/CCE attack procedures. The new few-shot analysis measures preservation on COCO-1K. Table D.8 becomes E.8 and corrects eta values from 0.3/0.5/3.0 to 1.0/5.0/1.0, matching existing prose; these corrections do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine gate parameters tau2 and u (Table C.8), generation counts for explicit-content erasure (Table D.2), and robustness against PEZ and CCE (Table D.4). These substantially broaden sensitivity and adversarial testing. Existing rank, concept-selection, timestep, and eta analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Existing generation-seed disclosures remain, without new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added generation-count ablation varies adaptation samples rather than reporting repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial result groups while retaining the numerical results in main Tables 1–5. New GLoCE results include PEZ/CCE attack success rates of 0.00%/30.99%, SD v3 Hcc values of 82.50/82.00, and airplane/dog Hcc values of 93.19/93.63. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects intermediate proof expressions: the bias uses the target mean instead of the mapping mean, and the second singular-value factor in the Q derivation changes from exponent 1/2 to -1/2. The final closed-form solution is retained; organizing the derivation into two lemmas mainly changes presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: localized concept erasure, training-free gated low-rank adaptation, improved fidelity and erasure performance, robustness, and mass-concept applicability. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 newly explains that larger tau2 or smaller u reduces gate discrimination. Appendix D interprets the new experiments as supporting applicability across diffusion backbones and object domains. The explicit-erasure efficacy–fidelity tradeoff was already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability link in the abstract and corrects the configuration table's rank, scale, concept-pool, and anchor information toward agreement with existing prose. Most prompt templates, seeds, generation counts, and hardware/runtime details were already present. Detailed setups for the new SD v3 and object experiments remain sparse.

R1.justification: Related work adds CPE and its nonlinear gating/specificity positioning, while new references support DiT, PEZ, and CCE evaluations. Continual-learning citations are also revised. The overall positioning relative to LEACE and existing concept-erasure approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 clarifies token-level notation and mapping explanations, restructures the proof into lemmas, and creates an additional quantitative-results appendix. Some headings and terminology become more explicit. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the SD v3 qualitative Figure 7, proof schematic Figure B.1, and new experimental tables. Figures 3 and 4 exchange positions, and appendix tables are regrouped. Existing qualitative appendix images are retained under new labels, with the overall visual format preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through direct LEACE comparisons, SD v3 and localized-object tests, additional attacks, and gate sensitivity studies. It also corrects reproducibility-relevant configuration inconsistencies and several proof expressions. These provide a clear net benefit, but the added experiments have limited setup documentation and retain the original uncertainty-reporting limitations, so the overall improvement is bounded.
